question: Should an exec auto-reviewer's low-risk verdict be reusable for repeated identical gateway executions, or must every `allow-once` result remain tied to one execution?
rationale: The current contract and original feature describe one-shot approval, while this optimization intentionally broadens one model judgment to multiple executions; code review cannot choose that authorization policy safely.

options.title: Add an explicit reusable verdict
options.body: Introduce a separately named run-scoped outcome with exact binding and lifecycle rules instead of overloading `allow-once`.

options.title: Accept gateway memoization
options.body: Approve the current bounded reuse semantics and update documentation and security tests to state that identical gateway requests may reuse one reviewer judgment.

options.title: Preserve one-shot review
options.body: Decline memoization and retain a fresh reviewer completion for every ask-requiring execution.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit reusable verdict
recommendation.body: Introduce a separately named run-scoped outcome with exact binding and lifecycle rules instead of overloading `allow-once`.

likelyOwner.reason: The original auto-mode authorship provides the strongest available ownership signal for choosing its authorization semantics.
